IMAGE — the champion poster, 1080 × 1350

Owner Q4: a champion poster anyone may share; names and photos allowed (F8's ADR)

Drawn on a <canvas> at 1080 x 1350 (4:5). Every size here is canvas px. Noor E. has a photo (an illustration stands in for a real one); the others show LiveCard's shirt back. The circle under each card is its night rating (ratings sample, so it replays the same world on today's engine; the path and final are the DR2 story).

IMAGE — my night, 1080 × 1350

Owner Q4: 'my night', your own five and path, with your five's night ratings

Sanne's path, her coins (wins + calls), her five with night ratings, and the best card's line exactly as the ratings function wrote it. Bas V. has a photo; the others the shirt back. A line never mocks a card, so a low night just shows its number.

/MIDWEEK — 21:08, the week complete

ADR-117 ratings once complete; ADR-118 weekly line; Q4 share; DR2 champion view

The DR2 placeholders are filled: 'Your five's ratings' best first, each with its line and a neutral circle (never tinted, so it can't be read as Power); the weekly calls line under Your night; and the share block with both previews. 'You' now adds wins and calls. Below lg one row per card; from lg the five LiveCards.

/MIDWEEK/2026-10-05 — the week's bracket once complete

Ratings outlive Thursday: the bracket keeps them; Show each match opened

The champion view leads only until Thursday 23:59 (D4); the week's bracket keeps your ratings for good. Here 'Show each match' is open: each card's match ratings, each a link to that match's report. Your calls and the share block sit here too.

/MIDWEEK/2026-10-05/MATCH/[ID] — a report after the week is complete

ADR-117 per-match ratings in MidweekWhyList, apart from the Power pill

Mila v Eline, 0-3 in both samples. Each card's rating for this match sits on the right as the same neutral circle; Power keeps its tinted pill on the left. A key above the list names both. Until the week is complete the column isn't there (DR2's list unchanged).

/MIDWEEK — 20:41, out, the semi-finals open

ADR-118: only members who are out; open once both feeders have ended; change until kick-off

Replaces the DR2 placeholder. Semi-final 1 is called and saved; semi-final 2 is open with no pick; the final opens when both semi-finals have ended. A tap saves at once (no submit). Cards are neutral: they list matches (DR2-1).

/MIDWEEK — every state of a call

ADR-118 Part L #28: open, change, close at kick-off; split from kick-off; own picks only

The block in each state, top to bottom: nothing open yet (Laura at 20:35, out while both other quarter-finals are still in their shoot-outs), open, saving, saved, changed, a refused save, closed at kick-off with the club's split, the final open, resolving, and the weekly line once the week is complete. Blue-grey labels are design notes, not app copy.

/MIDWEEK — 21:05, the final live, your calls

ADR-118: the split from kick-off; your picks resolve as matches end

The final leads for everyone (DR2). Below it, your calls: both semi-finals came true, the final is closed and shows how the club split (counts only). Coins for calls are paid with the rest after the final.

/MIDWEEK/2026-10-05 — 20:41, your calls on the bracket

Where else picking goes: the bracket shows your calls and links to them; it doesn't take picks

Recommendation: one place to pick (the evening page, where a member who is out already is), and the bracket shows each call on its row, with a jump link while one is open. Fewer places that save, one set of states to build and test.

/MIDWEEK — tapping Share (phone) or Download (desktop)

Owner Q4: Web Share on phones, a download on desktop; no server

Phones (320, 412): Share opens the phone's own share sheet with the PNG attached; WhatsApp is one tap. 'Save image' downloads instead. Desktop (1440): Download saves the PNG and says where it went. The image is drawn when the button is tapped, from data the page already has.

/MIDWEEK — saved, a balanced five

ADR-116: 3 plusses per line from the four not in goal; ×0.88 per plus short

A Goalkeeper, a Speedster, a Finisher, a Defender and an All-rounder: attack 6, midfield 5, defence 4. The count sits under the keeper check, above the save bar. Each list row shows the card's plusses as A/M/D.

/MIDWEEK — unsaved, defence 1 short

ADR-116; DR2's sticky save bar on phones

A Goalkeeper, a Speedster, a Finisher and two All-rounders: defence has 2 of 3, so the five plays at ×0.88. On a phone the sticky save bar carries the one-line verdict, so the cost is visible at the moment of saving even when the count has scrolled away.

/MIDWEEK — unsaved, no Goalkeeper: no count

Owner Q8 (3 Oct): no count until a Goalkeeper is picked

Without a Goalkeeper the stand-in is only settled at the lock (it depends on form), so the picker can't say which four count. It shows no count and says why; the sticky bar says the same in one line. The keeper check above already warns.

/MIDWEEK — unsaved, three keepers, two lines short

ADR-116; with the table, two lines short needs two Goalkeepers outfield

Three Goalkeepers and two All-rounders: one keeper in goal, two outfield at 0/0/3. Attack and midfield are each 1 short, 2 plusses in all: ×0.77. With today's table this is the only way to fall short in two lines.

/MIDWEEK — the same, without colour

Colour is never the only signal

The two-short five in greyscale: filled against dashed pips, the threshold tick after the third, the ✓ and ! marks and the words 'enough' and '1 short' all still say it.

TOKENS — violet and teal, and the checks

Owner, 3 Oct: 'deeper colours would be more classy'; round 2: 'an even darker / deeper red, or an alternative'

Chosen (owner, 3 Oct): violet and teal. Royal blue (round 2) kept for comparison. Text tones for names and numbers (AA on every surface), deep fills for everything drawn, Live on its own tokens. Ratios and colour-blind simulations are computed by the generator.
